Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off
Sports.content:
1 Nwaneri out of Arsenal picture

While Myles Lewis-Skelly looks likely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 New United pair down for Tigers test

Manchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch. Will Unwin

Hull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?

Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year. WU

Ipswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Emersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer. Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

4 Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debut

August is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed for Manchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.” Ben Fisher

Nottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

5 Serene Senesi can bring calm to Spurs

Cristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutral Premier League watchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs. WU

Brentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

6 Villa head south besieged by problems

It is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in? David Hytner

Brighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm

7 Maresca must win to silence City noise

Is Enzo Maresca already under pressure after Manchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenal in the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Anything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

8 King Kev remembered at Newcastle

Kevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute to one of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Liverpool, Sunday 4.30pm

9 Former Madrid managers meet in capital

Real Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. The Fulham man, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively. WU

Sports.title: Ronaldinho, 46, on mission of love and happiness – and maybe goals – at Serie C’s Ravenna
Sports.content:
It seemed like a joke, a hoax, when at 10pm on 19 June, Ravenna broke the news of Ronaldinho’s signing. The Brazilian, a former Ballon d’Or winner and one of the most recognisable figures in world football, had played his last official match in 2015 for Fluminense; a professional signing in Serie C at 46 years of age seemed unrealistic, to say the least. With football’s attention taken by the World Cup, the game was shocked by this bolt from the blue. For the most part, it remained in disbelief.

There was much discussion, in the city and around the world, about the real value of this operation, and we talked about it too, speaking with the mayor, the fans, and the president of Ravenna, Ignazio Cipriani, scion of the family known globally for Harry’s Bar, who is giving his city much more than a dream.

A dream that materialised, dispelling any doubts, at 11.50am on Thursday, when Ronaldinho, in a floral shirt and Bermuda shorts, with his now-familiar flat cap on his head, walked down the steps of the private jet that brought him from Milan Linate to the runway of Forlì airport. It is all true, all real. From there, he went on to the customary medical, like a true footballer. Ronaldinho is becoming a partner in the Ravenna club, as explained by the president, but he will also do his part on the pitch, with the dream of scoring the final goal of his career in the yellow-and-red jersey.

Then came the quick press conference, organised by the ownership at the Monaldina, the historic residence of the Gardini-Ferruzzi entrepreneurial family, the maternal dynasty from which Cipriani descends. There were few questions and hushed answers, very few words carefully chosen by Ronaldinho, who with his customary smile and gentle manners truly seems to have stepped back in time.

“The Milan derby is the most beautiful memory of my previous Italian experience,” began the former Barcelona and Milan No 10, before clarifying what drove him to Romagna: “Friendship and passion are the keys that brought me back here.”

He then clarified his goals in Ravenna: “To help, to excite the other players, and to have a spectacular season. To win, if possible.” Regarding his possible presence on the pitch, he explained: “If a goal comes, my experience in Ravenna will become even more beautiful, but whether I will actually play will be decided by the president and the coach.”

What does he think of the enthusiasm of Ravenna, a city that has literally gone crazy for him? Ronaldinho smiled and replied: “I just arrived, but I have a great desire to live this experience with the whole city.” His mission, he had already declared, is to bring happiness and love.

Echoing his words and capturing the essence of the city’s excitement was Ariedo Braida. Almost enunciating every word, the veteran executive summarised the operation with a striking remark: “We have the magic of football in Ravenna, what more could we ask for?”

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho salutes onlookers but he will not participate in Ravenna’s opening Serie C game on Monday. Photograph: Massimo Paolone/LaPresse/Shutterstock

The former Milan and Barcelona director also recalled the opinion expressed by Kevin-Prince Boateng in 2016, according to which Ronaldinho holds the top spot in a ranking that also includes Pelé, Maradona, Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Closing the circle was Cipriani himself, who revealed the behind-the-scenes of the miracle, after clarifying: “Ronaldinho is in shape.” When asked how he convinced the Brazilian champion, the answer was identical to that of the player: “Friendship and passion.” Cipriani then confirmed Ronaldinho’s entry as a shareholder in Ravenna FC, insisting on the profound meaning of the corporate move: “It’s not just about marketing, it’s not just international visibility. It is the chance to create a new enthusiasm around the club and the yellow-and-red jersey.”

Then the party began, organised in grand style on a stage set up on the beach at Marina di Ravenna, featuring the presentation of the entire Ravenna squad. The club’s president does not hide the ambition of a rapid climb to Serie B, with his sights set on the top flight. The star of the event, needless to say, was the Brazilian star, who for the first time presented himself before his new people, those Ravenna fans who back in June were curious, sceptical, or in disbelief.

Every doubt was dispelled on the beach of the ancient Byzantine capital, which today, with the arrival of the former Ballon d’Or winner, can truly dream big.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In living memory, the Romagnol city has never been talked about so much all over the world.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho’s unexpected comeback has captured fans’ imaginations, with 2,700 season tickets sold. Photograph: Stefano Rellandini/AFP/Getty Images

The fans didn’t just show up on the beach to celebrate their new idol, they also did so at the box office: the “Ronaldinho effect” has led to over 2,700 season tickets sold for Ravenna’s Serie C campaign, which kicks off on Monday in Reggio Emilia.

Ronaldinho, as confirmed by Cipriani, will not take part in the away match, but the fans hope to soon see him wearing the No 10 jersey, which was handed to him upon his arrival in Ravenna by the head coach, Andrea Mandorlini.

“Thank you very much,” are the words Ronaldinho dedicated to his celebrating people, while a child climbing the scaffolding of the giant screen shouted: “I saw him!”

He saw him at 46 years old, they had told him stories about him. Perhaps he will see him play again. This is the magic of football.

Sports.title: Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says it’s ‘ridiculous’ to suggest Manchester United have been handed an easy start to the season – and admits it’s asking a lot for his team to be considered title challengers.

United kick off the campaign at Hull City on Saturday lunchtime followed by a first home game against another of the newly-promoted teams, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford the following week.

But Carrick has rejected claims that United have been given an easy ride, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous.

‘It’s a tough start against both teams, but we’re not getting past Saturday. A newly-promoted team away from home will be a tough game.

‘That is the beauty of the new season. For teams coming up into the league, there tend to be quite a few changes. That is the challenge playing against them, we are fully aware of that. Mentally and physically we have done a lot of work. We are fully aware of what’s at stake and what’s coming at us.’

On United’s chances of delivering a first Premier League title since 2013 while coping with the demands of a Champions League return, Carrick added: ‘It’s going to be a jump. It doesn’t matter whether I say whether we can or can’t – and I would never say we can’t – it’s about what we can do, and what we are capable of doing as a group.

Carrick has rejected claims that United have been handed an easy start to the season, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous'

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba (right)

‘The run of form we had last season gives us confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make as a group. We have the potential to achieve things and we have to believe we can do good things.’

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, having already spent £85m on Andrey Santos, of Chelsea, and Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans. The club are also keen to strengthen at left-back.

Carrick was reluctant to say too much with another 11 days to go until the transfer window closes. ‘I just think we are looking to strengthen the squad, and we are working towards that,’ he said. ‘We’re certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it, and I think we are in a good way to doing that so far.’

Marcus Rashford’s return from a loan spell at Barcelona has given United another option, and Carrick has been delighted with the England international’s attitude so far.

‘It has been pretty obvious that Marcus came back training with Kobbie (Mainoo) and Licha (Martinez) that he has come back fantastically well,’ added the United boss. ‘He looks strong, sharp and ready to play football. He can play through the middle, even though it’s not his No 1 position. We have forwards that give us that flexibility.’

Carrick had some positive injury news with Mason Mount close to fitness after missing the final two friendlies against Leeds and AC Milan with a foot injury. Benjamin Sesko, Matthijs De Ligt and new No 2 goalkeeper Karl Darlow, none of whom featured in pre-season, are also back in training.

‘Karl has trained this week, he is in good shape,’ said Carrick. ‘Mattha has been out for a long period of time, but he is training, and it’s great to have him back. He won’t be involved but he is in good shape and moving in a good direction, so that is a bonus for us. Ben is back training so that is another positive and we’re looking forward to having him back around the group and getting him some minutes.

‘We’re managing Mason a little bit, but he is very close. He’s touch and go for the weekend really and going into next week. Mason will be back very, very soon, if not immediately, so it's all good.’

Sports.title: Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool are expected to make an improved offer for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh after having a £50m bid rejected.

The Gambian is out until October after undergoing surgery on his right leg.

Liverpool reverted to the 22-year-old after considering Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris St Germain too expensive. They are continuing discussions for Bradley Barcola.

Daily Mail Sport reported upon Mohamed Salah’s departure that the Gambia international would feature on a list to bolster the wide forward position this summer.

While talks for Barcola are ongoing, they would preferably like two forwards with Ibrahim Mbaye, also of PSG, one sounded out last week.

Minteh is currently on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Brighton's pre-season win over Roma earlier this month.

Liverpool have approached Brighton over signing winger Yankuba Minteh this summer

Andoni Iraola's side are in the market to sign two forwards, with the club locked in talks over PSG's Bradley Barcola

Minteh has made 73 appearances for Brighton to date since joining from Newcastle in a £30m move in the summer of 2024. He has scored 10 goals and provided nine assists for the Seagulls.

Minteh predominantly plays on the right wing, but has also been used on the left by Fabian Hurzeler.

Meanwhile, Curtis Jones will have a medical at noon on Friday after Liverpool agreed to sell him to Inter Milan for £26.7m plus £4m in bonuses and a 10 percent sell-on.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

Liverpool are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

Sports.title: RANGERS 1 JABLONEC 0: Ryan Naderi nets to nick a narrow lead but Ibrox men remain so unconvincing
Sports.content:
RANGERS 1 JABLONEC 0: Ryan Naderi nets to nick a narrow lead but Ibrox men remain so unconvincing

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

After taking a step forward with an emphatic victory over St Mirren in the Premier Sports Cup last weekend, this was a night when Rangers flirted with the idea of immediately taking two in the opposite direction.

In a UEFA Conference League play-off tie against Jablonec, Rangers made heavy weather of it - and then some.

A solitary goal from Ryan Naderi five minutes into the second half was enough to secure a one-goal lead as they head to the Czech Republic for next week's second leg.

But this is far from a done deal. Rangers remain far from convincing and no one can be sure that they will have group-stage football in Europe to look forward to for the season ahead.

The last time Rangers did not play in the group stage of a European competition was back in 2017 when they lost to Progres Niederkorn.

Derek McInnes and his players still have it all to do. Even against such limited opposition, Rangers were not impressive for the most part.

Ryan Naderi sees his effort hit the roof of the net to ensure Rangers take a first-leg lead

Rangers are denied as Jablonec defended stoutly at Ibrox

They were laborious in possession and largely devoid of creativity. They are still in the market for two new wingers and a new striker is possible.

It's not difficult to see why. The problem for McInnes is that he has already signed 11 new players. This is now very much his team and there looks to be precious little cohesion or attacking threat.

Rangers were clinging on towards the end after Cammy Devlin was shown a straight red card barely two minutes after coming off the bench.

It was a decision with which he could have no complaints, given it was high and it endangered his opponent.

If McInnes is to make a success of this job, it's difficult to overstate how important next week's return leg will be.

By hook or by crook, he and his players must come through it. If they were to be dumped out of Europe in two separate competitions by Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec, it would be a major blot on his copybook.

Even this early in his tenure, he is fighting to convince some supporters he is the right man for the job. There is absolutely no style or identity to this team whatsoever.

Rangers were marginally improved in the second half but the overall paucity of the performance left the Ibrox crowd flat and underwhelmed, despite the slender victory.

When the Rangers team-sheet dropped prior to kick-off, more than a few eyebrows would have been raised at the fact Lawrence Shankland was once again on the bench.

McInnes had spoken pre-match about Shankland and insisted that he retained full confidence in the striker's ability to make a success of himself at Ibrox.

Yet, in a game of this magnitude, with European group-stage football on the line, there was something odd about the newly-appointed club captain not being in the starting XI.

Having deployed the team in a 4-3-3 shape in the 5-1 thrashing of St Mirren last weekend, McInnes clearly liked what he saw and stuck with it.

Naderi celebrates his goal, which could prove to be invaluable next week

Perhaps that's what went against Shankland, whose lack of mobility and ability to press makes him ill-suited to play the lone striker role in this system.

It was Ryan Naderi who got the nod up front, with the only change seeing Dan Neil coming in as captain to replace Nico Raskin in midfield.

For all they may not be the most glamorous of names to have graced Ibrox over the years, Jablonec arrived in confident mood on the back of six straight wins in all competitions.

The Czechs were quite content to sit in and frustrate Rangers in the early stages. In fairness, given the lack of creativity in the home side, it probably wasn't the most difficult of tasks.

Rangers lacked any guile or tempo in possession. Everything they did was one-paced and predictable, moving the ball from side to side, without any hint of penetration.

Manny Fernandez has been in poor form so far this season and it was notable just how nervous the crowd became when he was on the ball.

There looks to be a mistake in him at any moment. He picked up a booking after only 10 minutes and had to walk a tightrope for the remainder of the match.

As soon as Ben Godfrey is fit again, it is surely inevitable that he will come back into the team to partner Olwethu Makhanya and Fernandez will be dropped.

Rangers finally mustered a sight of goal on 25 minutes when some neat play in the penalty box saw Naderi lay the ball off to Vanja Dragojevic.

The Serbian midfielder had scored a screamer against St Mirren last weekend, but, on this occasion, his shot came back off the post and trickled along the goalline before the visitors were able to clear their lines.

Fernandez continued to be a bag of nerves. His body language was dreadful at times, moaning at others around him even though it was he who had made the mistake.

If there was a sense that the emphatic victory over St Mirren last weekend might imbue Rangers with a renewed sense of confidence, it simply did not materialise.

There were booed off at half-time. What made the performance so unimpressive was the fact that Jablonec were there for the taking.

Cammy Devlin saw red moments after coming on for Rangers as a second-half substitute

The Czechs could kindly be described as limited opposition. Even a semi-competent Rangers team would have been able to brush them aside with ease.

But this was another slog. The onus was on McInnes as manager to impart some kind of meaningful change heading into the second half.

With the crowd growing ever more restless, the breakthrough duly arrived within five minutes of the restart to ease the tension.

With what felt like his first forward pass all night, Neil clipped a ball to the back post, where Daisuke Yokota cushioned a header back across the face of goal.

With the goalkeeper out of position, Naderi, who had been largely anonymous, had the simple task of tapping home into the empty net.

The goal breathed new life into Rangers and it really ought to have been 2-0 just five minutes later when they cut the Czechs open down the right.

It was Naderi who whipped in a good cross to the far post for Djeidi Gassama. He met the ball first time on the volley and blazed it over when heading it may have been the better option.

Knowing that a one-goal lead would make for a nervy affair next week in the Czech Republic, Rangers were desperate to try and build on it if possible.

McInnes made a double change on 69 minutes, bringing on Devlin and Findlay Curtis as he tried to inject some fresh legs.

But it proved to be a disastrous cameo from Devlin, who, having only been on the pitch for a couple of minutes, went in late and high on Jablonec left-back Jiri Slama.

Romanian referee Marian Barbu appeared to miss the incident initially, but, after being referred to the monitor by the VAR, he showed Devlin a straight red card.

This was desperate for Rangers. It was now a case of backs to the wall and trying to cling on against a team who would be no more than mid-table in the Scottish Premiership.

They got the job done in the end, but it was a tough watch. Truth be told, they will settle for more of the same next week if the end result is a place in the group stage.

Sports.title: Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Man United progressing in Baleba talks Manchester United are continuing discussions over a fee with Brighton for Carlos Baleba. Brighton have rejected United’s £60million plus £5m for the midfielder but talks have been progressing to a compromise. The 22-year-old Cameroon international is hoping the deal can be wrapped up over the weekend. Meanwhile, United right-back Habeeb Ogunneye is scheduled to undergo a medical with Arsenal ahead of his move there. The deal is understood to be a free transfer with 40percent sell-on clause. The 20-year-old is being signed to boost numbers with Arsenal’s U21s but also train with the first team. Man United have had a £65m offer for Carlos Baleba rejected but talks are progressing with Brighton Clubs circle for Jackson Atletico Madrid have enquired about a loan deal for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson. Atletico director Mateu Alemany was understood to have travelled to London on Thursday for talks. Jackson also has interest from Aston Villa, Napoli and Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile Chelsea forward Deivid Washington is a target for Marseilla, Strasbourg and Sevilla. Blues defender Axel Disasi is continuing to discuss a loan move to Crystal Palace while Benoit Badiashile is joining Napoli. Leeds United are interested in striker Liam Delap as are Everton. Spurs talk numbers Tottenham are working on figures with City for Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. The deal for Savinho could be worth up to £84m. City have also asked about Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton as they work through a list of targets. Leeds swoop for goalkeeper Zetterer Leeds United are closing on a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer to come in as James Trafford's deputy. The clubs are finalising agreement for the 31-year-old, but Frankfurt need to find a new goalkeeper to replace Zetterer first. Leeds are waiting for Lucas Perri to fully recover from a minor injury before he completes his delayed loan move to Torino. Zetterer, 31, is a former Germany U21 international. Southampton reject Villa approach for Harwood-Bellis Aston Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis. Villa are willing to offer around £17.5m for the 24-year-old but Saints had already rejected a similar offer from Benfica. Talks are ongoing as Villa assess options such as Tosin Adarabioyo at Chelsea and Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan to fill the void left by Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal. Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis City keep watching brief on Wharton Manchester City maintain an interest in Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. The Selhurst Park club are reluctant to lose the 22-year-old this summer but have been making significant enquiries for midfielders in recent weeks. City are exploring several options including Manu Kone at Roma while they are advancing in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are assessing the cost of a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez. 'We did it [sold big players in the past], and now is not the moment to do that,' said Palace boss Pierre Sage on Thursday. 'He is able to play in another club, a big club. Here, or anywhere in Europe, but one year with us, in a new dynamic, will be good for him. And we need him - that is why I think he will stay with us.' Wharton has been a significant Premier League performer in recent seasons and excelled in the Europa League Conference final but analysts at some top level would-be suitors have indicated his running statistics do not reflect someone who can fit into a high-pressing style. He continues to show on the pitch, however, an ability to find the right pass and shield his defence. City have also made contact with Palmeiras for winger Allan Elias as they seek a replacement for Savinho. Allan, 22, wants to join City but his club are reluctant to sell now with their season running to December. Talks are ongoing over a £35million fee. SIMON JONES AND BOBBY MANZI Manchester City have seen an enquiry for Adam Wharton rebuffed by Crystal Palace Jones set for Inter medical Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to arrive later today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. The Italian side have scheduled Jones' medical for midday on Friday. Inter bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham. Curtis Jones is set to sign a five-year deal with Inter Jones, 25, will sign a five-year deal with the Serie A champions. Meanwhile, Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, is in talks to join Levante on loan. Ndukwe does not qualify for a work permit in England so must be loaned out. Liverpool remain in talks over PSG winger Bradley Barcola. Sheffield Wednesday are to confirm the signing of Liverpool's Northern Ireland international winger Kieran Morrison on a season-long loan. Hammers close on Mukasa West Ham are close to an agreement to sign highly-rated Manchester City forward Divine Mukasa on loan for the season. There is no buy option for the 18-year-old who spent the second half of last season on loan at Leicester City City step up hunt for Savinho replacement Manchester City have asked about Palmeiras winger Allan Elias as they consider replacements for Savinho. Allan is 22 but has not been capped by Brazil. Quick and skilful, he is not a goalscorer but has earned a reputation as a worker, willing to press. Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also scouted him in recent months. City are evaluating several options with Tottenham working on the deal to sign Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. Bayern reach Palhinha agreement Bayern Munich have reached a full agreement with Benfica over the £17million sale of Joao Palhinha. The 31-year-old midfielder had been a target for Aston Villa and Newcastle United but will now reunite with his former Fulham boss Marco Silva at Benfica. Villa were only willing to take him on an initial loan which Bayern refused. Villa table new contract offer to Watkins Aston Villa have made a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins. The 30-year-old is open to a move to Al Hilal who had a £38.5m offer rejected on Tuesday but are preparing a fourth offer for the England international. Watkins has scored consistently throughout his Villa career and his goals would be difficult to replace. Villa have maintained contacts over Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson who also has interest from Napoli but he is valued around £65m. Aston Villa have put forward a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins Wrexham make move for ex-United star Wrexham are continuing discussions with free agent Axel Tuanzebe. The 28-year-old Congo international left Burnley at the end of last season and has had interest from clubs but is interested in Wrexham's ambitious project. The 22-year-old was discussed as an option in January and Palace have made further enquiries. The France U21 international is an attacking player who can also play out wide and was on Newcastle United's list earlier in the year. Hull advance in talks for Betis star Garcia Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has confirmed they are making progress on their bid to sign Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia and remain in talks for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez. 'I think probably, if nothing unknown happens, we will see him in a black and gold shirt. It has to be finalised, but I would say 90 percent of this deal is done. We are talking about the last details,' said Ilicali. Pictures of Hernandez in Hull have been posted on social media, and Ilicali told BBC Humberside: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. 'He is a young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.' He made one appearance in the FA Cup against Oxford United and then started against Fulham in the Premier League. Sports.title: HEARTS 2 RAPID VIENNA 2: Wilson's wonder strike has Tynecastle in raptures but Gorgie men are pegged back for draw
Sports.content:
Hearts’ hopes of avoiding the ignominy of being knocked out of three different European competitions in the space of six weeks at the start of the season are in the balance following a dramatic night in Gorgie.

After trailing to Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao’s goal at the interval, a stirring second half display looked like it might be enough to take a lead to Vienna for the second leg of their Conference League play-off round tie.

Josh McPake’s equaliser and a sensational strike from James Wilson - a goal which will live long in Hearts folklore - put Wouter Vrancken’s side in front and had Tynecastle rocking.

Hearts striker James Wilson celebrates after scoring a 30-yard screamer

Austrian Bundesliga leaders Rapid reinstated themselves as firm favourites to reach the league phase of the competition, however, when sub Nikolaus Wurmbrand restored parity in the closing stages.

Hearts now have it all to do in the second leg next Wednesday if they are to avoid that unwanted hat-trick after already losing in the qualifying rounds of the Champions League and Europa League.

Having already conceded 13 times over the course of those ties against Sturm Graz and Benfica, trying to tighten up defensively was an obvious priority for Hearts.

That was never going to be easy against a free-wheeling Rapid outfit who arrived in Edinburgh having racked up 29 goals in winning all eight of their competitive matches so far this season.

It didn’t take them long to showcase their attacking prowess with only an exceptional piece of goalkeeping from Beau Reus preventing Hearts from falling behind after just nine minutes.

Rapid weaved their way into the home penalty area with pace and precision to leave Matthias Seidl one-on-one with the Hearts keeper. The Rapid captain struck his shot cleanly enough but was denied by a superb save from Reus.

The big Dutchman was called into action again three minutes later and once again was up to the task. Jannes Horn found space on the left to clip in a cross which Bendeguz Bolla met with a crisp header on the edge of the six yard box.

James Wilson lets fly from distance to put Hearts 2-1 up against Rapid Vienna

Rapid’s Hungarian defender was already in the throes of celebrating what looked like a certain goal when Reus threw himself to his left and somehow clawed the ball away to safety.

Claudio Braga did his best to ease the early anxiety and lift the mood of the Hearts support. Regardless of persistent speculation he will be sold by Hearts before the summer transfer window closes, there has been no drop-off in the work rate and commitment which made Braga Scotland’s Player of the Year last season.

The Portuguese forward got Hearts onto the front foot for a spell with his powerful running and clever positional play. Unfortunately, it wasn’t matched by central striker Pierre Landry Kabore whose tendency to dwell just too long in possession earned him the groans and moans of the home fans.

Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao scores the opening goal for Rapid Vienna

At the other end of the pitch, Hearts continued to invite their own problems. Rapid had clearly identified Jordi Altena as a potential weak link and the Hearts right-back did nothing to confound that assessment.

Altena, not for the first time, was careless in possession when he played a blind pass across the face of his own defensive third in the 28th minute. It went straight to Tonni Adamsen but, fortunately for Hearts, the Danish striker couldn’t take advantage as his tame shot was comfortably held by Reus.

Despite that warning shot, Altena failed to learn his lesson and it proved damaging for Hearts as they fell behind two minutes later.

Altena coughed up possession needlessly once more, forcing team-mate Oisin McEntee to mop up after him at the expense of a corner. Bolla took it from the left, picking out Seidl on the edge of the box.

He flicked it on to Raux-Yao who had all the time and space he could wish for to head past Reus from close range. A lengthy VAR check suggested there might be a reprieve for Hearts but the big defender had indeed stayed just onside.

The goal inevitably deflated the mood inside Tynecastle but Hearts rallied towards the end of the first half to offer some indication they were capable of finding a way back into the tie.

McPake cut in from the left and drilled in a low shot which Rapid goalkeeper Niklas Hedl did well to clutch at his right hand post.

Braga and Tom Renaud also tried their luck from distance, the former’s effort flying narrowly wide before the latter forced another save from Hedl.

That promise of better things to come was fulfilled as Hearts made a vibrant start to the second half, cranking up a spell of pressure which saw them stun Rapid and overturn the interval deficit.

Hearts winger Josh McPake scores to make it 1-1 at Tynecastle

Braga continued to provide the spark and was unlucky to see a shot deflected just wide of Hedl’s right hand post.

Kabore finally followed his lead and made a worthy contribution to Hearts’ 56th minute equaliser with a clever reverse pass to set McPake free on the left of Rapid’s penalty area. The former St Johnstone winger steadied himself and curled in a shot which took a wicked deflection off Raux-Yao to leave Hedl helpless as the ball flew into the top of his net.

It was Kabore’s last involvement before he was replaced by Wilson. As Hearts looked to make the most of the momentum now with them, Jamie McCart sent a header agonisingly wide of Hedl’s left hand post from a Blair Spittal corner.

The home team’s second goal was on the way, however, and was worth waiting for. It’s one which will be fondly recalled in Gorgie for a long time to come.

There appeared to be little danger to Rapid when Wilson gathered the ball 30 yards out after a long clearance from Reus. Spotting Hedl off his line, however, the striker smashed a magnificent shot over him and into the top left hand corner of the net.

Sadly for Wilson and Hearts, it wasn’t the winner it richly deserved to be. Rapid regained control in the final 20 minutes and deserved to make it 2-2 when Wurmbrand’s shot was deflected beyond Reus after Hearts passed up several chances to clear a corner.

Sports.title: TNT Sport bosses bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game - as Tigers owner hits back
Sports.content:
Joe Cole has sparked a furious response from Hull City fans after claiming the Tigers are already relegated - and saying he put his phone on ‘do not disturb’ to ensure he would not have to be a pundit for TNT Sports at their season opener against Manchester United tomorrow night. The former Chelsea and England man has triggered outrage in East Yorkshire thanks to comments he made with former West Ham team-mate Carlton Cole on a podcast. When asked who would be going down this season, Cole said ‘Hull are gone, man’ before claiming that they had arrived in the Premier League ‘through the back door’. He then added that he had ‘a confession to make’, saying he had been contacted by TNT Sports who ‘tried to slip in Hull on the first day of the season’. ‘I put my phone on Do Not Disturb,’ he said. Hull City are GOING DOWN! 🗣️🐯 The lads don’t rate Hull’s chances this season 🥺 Watch in full 👉 https://t.co/PuonqV3D90#TheDressingRoom #PremierLeague #PL pic.twitter.com/B1xa8RV4nI — The Dressing Room Podcast (@dressingroomaa) August 19, 2026 Joe Cole has risked the wrath of Hull City fans with comments made on his podcast

Your browser does not support iframes.

Daily Mail Sport understands the comments have left bosses at TNT Sports bemused, with insiders saying Cole was not down to cover the opener at the MKM Stadium, and never had been. Regardless, it has stoked plenty of emotion in Hull. Sources have disclosed that players and staff are well aware of what was said and intend to use it as motivation for what would appear to be a tough mission ahead. Fans have taken to social media to highlight what they see as a ‘condescending’ and ‘disrespectful’ attitude, with some even claiming the newly-promoted club, who won the Championship play-off final, should ban Cole from its stadium. Hull owner Acun Ilicali responded to the comments from both Coles on social media, writing: 'It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better. 'As a club we are used to being underestimated and we enjoy it, and we enjoyed it more when were promoted last season. 'The true beauty of a place is in its people, and that’s why, for me, Hull is one of the most beautiful places in the world. 'For me, seeing two ex-players making fun of a deservedly promoted club, is more laughable than the things they were laughing at.'

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso refuses to rule out Enzo Fernandez exit with Chelsea set to demand MORE than £120m asking price for star man after Man City missed transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refuses to rule out Enzo Fernandez exit with Chelsea set to demand MORE than £120m asking price for star man after Man City missed transfer deadline

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Xabi Alonso refused to guarantee that Enzo Fernandez will be staying this summer – but believes he can overcome the Chelsea boo-boys if he does not depart for Manchester City.

Fernandez received a mixed reaction in their final friendly at Stamford Bridge before the Premier League begins. The 25-year-old Argentinian replaced Reece James against Real Sociedad – and took the captain’s armband – as he was both jeered and cheered by his own fans.

Speaking on the eve of the 2026-27 season starting, and with Chelsea away at Fulham on Monday, Alonso said: 'It's not unusual. It can happen. We support him. We have a great player with Enzo, a top player, so important. I am happy that when I see him training, you see that he has a competitive mentality. We work with him every day very well.’

Alonso also hinted Fernandez would remain his vice-captain under James. Asked if he can see Chelsea’s supporters getting behind the midfielder, Alonso added: ‘I’m sure it will happen because this is a normal situation in football. Once we start the competition, we need the support.

‘We need the full commitment of all the team and of all the supporters when they come to Stamford Bridge. That we are pushing in the same direction.’

Xabi Alonso has refused to be drawn on whether Enzo Fernandez will be a Chelsea player when the transfer window closes

City's interest in Fernandez has been no secret this summer, though the side managed by Enzo Maresca have yet to submit a formal offer for the Argentina international. Chelsea were previously asking for £120million, but the Blues say those terms expired with the deadline they set for bids last Friday. City could be quoted a higher asking price if they sought one now.

Alonso dodged answering any and all questions about whether Fernandez would be staying with Chelsea at his pre-Fulham press conference, choosing instead to highlight how well he is training.

‘Enzo is a Chelsea player,’ Alonso said when asked directly if Fernandez would still be with Chelsea beyond deadline day. ‘He's a top, top player. He's training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he's getting ready for Monday.

‘He's training really well. I see him with a good attitude. That's what we want. He’s a player, he’s training well, he’s preparing for Monday and that’s my concern at the moment.’

Fernandez was previously used as a No 10 at Chelsea, though Alonso did hint he sees him in a deeper role rather than competing with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

‘He can do both,’ Alonso said. ‘I think when he's with the ball, he has the qualities to link the short passes but the long ones as well. He's able to see short and the farther players and from there he can progress. But he’s played great as a No 10 as well.’

Sports.title: No ego, refreshingly candid and the polar opposite of Oliver Glasner: This is what I learned from Pierre Sage's brilliant first press conference as Crystal Palace boss - from his tactical 'three pillars' to transfer clues on Sarr, Wharton and more
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace's press suite has benefitted from a luxurious summer refurbishment. Not only have the plastic chairs better suited to a school classroom been replaced by rows of leather seating, there is also a new man in the hotseat.

Palace have erased any lasting memories of Oliver Glasner – who switched allegiances to their new rivals Nottingham Forest – changing the layout of the room, the screens and brutally ripping the photo of the Austrian celebrating the club's FA Cup win off the wall.

In his place sat Pierre Sage, the French coach who secured Champions League football at Lens last season and won the French Cup. An intelligent, dignified and sincere communicator.

Sage sat with the media for 40 minutes on Thursday, and the main takeaway was this: he could not be more different to his predecessor.

There are just two striking similarities between Sage and Glasner – they play the same formation and are fascinated by social science. Sage, after all, lectured on sports mentality for 10 years at Claude Bernard University in Lyon.

Even in his first Premier League press conference, the differences between Crystal Palace's new boss Pierre Sage (pictured) and his predecessor Oliver Glasner were evident

Glasner's dealings with the media were often spiky last season, as he complained whenever he didn't get his way

At the start of the year, Glasner's interactions with the press were spiky. He frequently played mind games with the club and its supporters, throwing his toys out of the pram – rightly or wrongly – whenever he did not get his own way. It was box office but draining.

Sage, on the other hand, was refreshing. There was no equivocating, just candid conversation. Despite admitting he is a reserved character, he sat down and exuded a genuine transparency.

'I’m quiet, shy, maybe,' Sage said. 'But when I speak and I’m hungry, they know.'

Perhaps that is because he is not a product of the football establishment. There was no professional playing career, he had nothing handed to him. Sage was an amateur footballer and coach with an aspiration shared by millions: elite football.

'Four or five years ago, my dream was to become a member of staff – not a manager – at a pro team... I did it,' Sage added. 'But I did it in a way I didn’t consider and I became a head coach. It works well. That’s why I told myself I needed a new dream, and two years ago that dream became coming to the Premier League. Now I am here. I have to build another dream.

'I’m a flag bearer of the amateur coach and for young coaches to give them hope to become a head coach of a good team, a professional team. You need to work every day. To have an opportunity, you have to be an opportunity yourself.

'I came from the bottom. Now I’m here, I just want to give my best. I have no pressure. For me, the pressure is giving the players the best session I can give every day. Sometimes there will be a gap between what we did in game and what we chose before the game. But our job is to make the gap as small as we can, improve the way we play and develop our game.'

'Two years ago my dream became coming to the Premier League,' said Sage. 'Now I am here. I have to build another dream'

Sage accepted it may take a while to place his imprint on the team, with staggered arrivals throughout pre-season because 13 Palace players were at the World Cup. But he will adopt Glasner's style of play to an extent and gradually integrate his ideas to ensure Palace get off to the best start possible.

That was not laying the groundwork for an excuse, though, just pragmatism. He still expects results from himself and his team from week one, starting at Everton on Saturday.

'We have to consider the late arrivals of the players and accept what the players are able to do collectively now,' Sage added. 'But we want to implement our principles because that will give us more options to win games.

'We will do that session after session, game after game. The most important thing is to play as a team, respect every moment of play and every moment of the game because we want to play as a unit.

'I always speak about three pillars. The first is about pressing, we want to recover the ball as soon as we can because we want to play with the ball and be efficient in build-up, creating good possession conditions in the opponents' half. At the end, we want to attack the depths (high areas) and put pressure, psychological pressure and space pressure on the opponents in games.

'We are able to do that in transition and by having the ball in possession. We want to be able to play in a lot of contexts to compete. We have a focus on set-pieces because they’re important to win games and make a difference in some moments.'

Could transfer exits rock the boat?

As far as Sage is concerned, Adam Wharton, Ismaila Sarr and Daniel Munoz will all remain at Palace beyond the closure of the summer transfer window.

Manchester City enquired for Wharton but were knocked back, with Palace maintaining he is not for sale. In any case, their current valuation of the midfielder exceeds £100million.

Meanwhile, Galatasaray had a bid north of £30million turned down for Sarr this week. Palace value the Senegal international significantly above his market value.

Everton have assessed Munoz, although they are currently exploring moves for other targets at right back.

Besides Romain Esse, who Sage explicitly stated was not a part of his plans, the Palace boss is looking to build his squad, not dismantle it further. Daily Mail Sport understands Palace want to add two centre backs and a midfielder before the window closes.

Manchester City have shown interest in Palace midfielder Adam Wharton but the club are adamant he's not for sale

'We will, we will,' Sage responded when asked if Palace will keep Sarr. 'He’s a really important player for the club and for us. He played in the World Cup with Senegal and joined the group three weeks ago. He will be able to play this weekend.'

'We did it (sold players) and now it’s not the moment to do that,' he said of Wharton's future. 'He is able to play in another club, a big club, here or anywhere in Europe. But one year with us and a new dynamic will be good for him. We need him and that’s why he will stay with us. I hope he continues his improvement.'

As for Munoz, Sage was blunt: 'I hear the noise but he is happy to be with us and we are happy he is here.'

He applied the pressure on the recruitment team, too, urging them to sign a centre back with Premier League experience. Palace are in talks to loan Axel Disasi from Chelsea.

Palace will start the Premier League season without a central centre back after Maxence Lacroix joined Chelsea. They are also yet to secure a replacement for Marc Guehi, who left the club seven months ago.

Glasner would have used that as a stick to beat the board with. It became his transfer window trademark, lambasting the board for sluggish business.

Sage, instead, made his point – but with humility. Whether a level-headed approach will work with Palace chairman Steve Parish remains to be seen; Glasner's rants often sprang him into action.

Deep down, Sage will be annoyed he is starting the season with an incomplete backline but publicly he toed the party line and said he would rather wait for the right option. The sign of a leader without ego.

Does Matheus Franca have a future at Palace?

It has been a tough three years for Matheus Franca since arriving at Palace. He signed for £17million as a promising teenager from Brazil and took Wilfried Zaha's number 11 shirt.

The expectations were high for a player most knew nothing about and he subsequently faltered at every opportunity. He has played just 14 league games for Palace, spending most of the time injured or out of favour.

Last season, he went back to Brazil to join Vasco da Gama on loan. He did not set the world alight there either.

But there has been a glimpse of the player Palace had such high hopes for in pre-season, with Franca scoring four times and looking comfortable playing as a No9 rather than his usual position out wide.

Matheus Franca has had a difficult sime since moving to Palace from Brazil as a teenager, but his performances in pre-season have been encouraging

New manager Sage believes all is not lost on Franca: 'He had a good pre-season with four goals. It was difficult for him as he began here, that’s why he went on loan to Brazil last year.

'He has to adapt to European football because it’s really different to South American football. He’s shown really good things and we will see what we will do with him. We have to build the best context for him to improve because he’s young but he has talent.'

Where does Cheick Doucoure fit in?

Cheick Doucoure has not played a competitive game in 18 months after rupturing his ACL just a year after recovering from an achilles injury. The midfielder, once touted with a £70million move to Liverpool, has had multiple years shaved off his career.

Yet after a stable pre-season, he is back at Palace's disposal and ready to play in the Premier League. It will take time before he is anywhere near his best. There is a chance he will never be the same player he was. Nevertheless, Sage is excited to work with an 'incredible player'.

'He’s able to start,' said Sage. 'He didn’t play much during the last two seasons so we have to consider him within this situation. He needs time to come back and we will take our time to let him in a good context, particularly on the psychological side.

'When you play, you have to be confident, understand this moment is only a step and in a few moments you will be the player you were two years ago. That’s why we will take our time with him.

'He understands that. He walks a lot around the session but he’s really happy to be on the pitch and we are happy to see him on the pitch because he’s an incredible player.'

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York

Joshua has insisted he wants the all-British heavyweight showdown to take place at Wembley, but Netflix and the Saudi Arabian moneymen behind the fight want to stage it in the Big Apple

View Image Anthony Joshua has made his demands

Anthony Joshua has submitted his demands to move his fight with Tyson Fury to New York.

‌



Joshua has insisted he wants the all-British heavyweight showdown to take place at Wembley. But Netflix and the Saudi Arabian moneymen behind the fight want to stage it in the Big Apple. It is understood Joshua is willing to face Fury at Madison Square Garden on November 20 if he is compensated financially.

‌



The former two-time world champion will face a hike in his tax bill if the bout is moved across the Atlantic and wants his purse increased to reflect that. Joshua is also understood to be owed money from his come-from-behind knockout win over Kristrian Prenga last month. Additionally, promoter Eddie Hearn has sought assurances over ticketing and security for the event, as reported by Boxing Scene.

‌



Joshua and Fury signed separate contracts for the fight earlier this year but only Joshua's deal included a demand over the venue. He believes hosting the biggest fight in British boxing history in America will damage his legacy. But he is now ready to relent in order to bring an end to his decade-long feud with rival Fury. If Joshua's demands are met, an official announcement could follow next week.

Tyson Fury drops biggest Anthony Joshua fight hint yet after ultimatum READ MORE :

Joshua's demands come after Fury's manager Spencer Brown expressed his concern over the delay in announcing the fight. "Everybody's got a bit of doubt in their mind," he said in an interview with Sky Sports. "There's reasons you could think that. If you'd asked me a week ago, I'd have said no, but now it's a little bit concerning that things haven't progressed down the line. We need to get this fight on."

Article continues below

"You can't keep flogging a dead horse, can you? We've been flogging a dead horse for months now. We've waited and waited to do it at Wembley. The hope is fading that it's going to be at Wembley.

"A decision must be made. Let's get the fight on wherever it is, whether it's in Timbuktu or whether it's in Wembley Stadium. We just want to get it announced. People are getting bored. We're in danger of really boring people."

Sports.title: Match of the Day legend fears for iconic show in major warning to BBC bosses
Sports.content:
Match of the Day legend fears for iconic show in major warning to BBC bosses

The BBC have announced more changes to Match of the Day, with the show continuing to evolve in the post-Gary Lineker era which in turn has sparked fears over its long-term future

View 2 Images Mark Lawrenson fears for Match of the Day (Image: Malcolm Couzens/Getty Images)

Match of the Day legend Mark Lawrenson has warned the BBC that the iconic show could end up suffering the same fate as Football Focus. The Beeb axed Football Focus after 52 years in May, with the corporation reshaping its football coverage.

‌



On Wednesday, chiefs announced more changes ahead of the new Premier League season, this time to its line-up for Match of the Day. Familiar faces Martin Keown, Dion Dublin, Shay Given, Stephen Warnock, Nedum Onuoha and Theo Walcott were all not named on their list of pundits, although Mirror Football understands that they will still play a role for MOTD in the 2026-27 campaign.

‌



Meanwhile, newcomers Ashley Young, Robbie Keane, Toby Alderweireld and Thomas Frank will join the show. Last season saw a new set of hosts, with Mark Chapman, Kelly Cates and Gabby Logan stepping in to replace the long-serving Gary Lineker following his abrupt departure after a fallout with BBC bosses.

‌



Assessing the state of Match of the Day four years after he exited the BBC, Lawrenson penned a column for the Telegraph. While he praised the show's new hosts, the former Liverpool defender wrote: "My worry is that there are now so many vehicles out there for the most insightful pundits - especially with the growth of podcasts such as Gary's - why would anyone feel an obligation to stay if they are worried about the direction of Match of the Day?

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There may come a point when questions such as, 'what is happening here?' will be asked, and other offers will feel more attractive. How long before they say, 'get me out of here?' It looks like it is already happening."

Lawrensen added: "Like all the best football shows, what attracts viewers is the familiarity of the personalities offering their insights. You may not always agree with them, but when they have authority, respect and gravitas you will still tune in to hear what they have to say."

Lineker already has a new gig, with his The Rest is Football podcast being shown on Netflix during the World Cup as part of a £14million deal, and it'll also be streamed on the platform throughout the new season. Lineker was joined in New York by ex-MOTD colleagues Alan Shearer and Micah Richards, whereas the BBC presented most of their coverage from Salford.

‌



Do you agree with Mark Lawrenson? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Mark Chapman, Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates are Match of the Day's hosts (Image: BBC)

Lawrenson labelled the decision 'nuts' and claimed that it sent a 'bad signal' to staff. "I could not believe the BBC's approach to the World Cup, with the presenting team based in Salford for the majority of the tournament while Gary and his two former BBC colleagues - Alan and Micah Richards - were in the US," the 69-year-old said.

Article continues below

"I know care has to be taken with budgets, but it's the World Cup for God's sake. That was nuts and it sends out a bad signal about priorities."

Sports.title: Man Utd's Carlos Baleba deal shows they've learnt from Frenkie de Jong mistake
Sports.content:
Man Utd's Carlos Baleba deal shows they've learnt from Frenkie de Jong mistake

Manchester United are closing in on signing Brighton's Carlos Baleba in another fast-moving piece of transfer business, unlike their days of chasing Frenkie de Jong to no avail

View 2 Images Manchester United tried to get Frenkie de Jong in 2022 (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

No galactico signings, no tedious sagas. Is this really a Manchester United transfer window?

‌



There was plenty of noise going into the summer about United's midfield rebuild, yet they've gone about their business relatively quietly. Andrey Santos' move from Chelsea came out of the blue, while the decision to trigger Youri Tielemans' £35million release clause made for another smooth transaction.

‌



Now Carlos Baleba is in line to become United's next rapid-fire signing. Prior to Wednesday's news that the Red Devils had submitted a £65m bid, reports suggested that the Brighton midfielder was no longer a priority, with the likes of Sander Berge, Manu Kone and Aurelien Tchouameni said to be preferred.

‌



Instead, they've sprung a surprise and quickly made progress on Baleba. It's a stark contrast to how United operated in the summer of 2022 when their public pursuit of Frenkie de Jong highlighted their lacklustre transfer strategy and ended in predictable failure.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



United went about their move for De Jong in quite literal broad daylight. CEO Richard Arnold and sporting director John Murtagh - each of them no longer at the club - were spotted in Barcelona in mid-July 2022 before reaching an agreement in principle for De Jong.

That was only club-to-club, however, and the Dutchman's reluctance to join the Red Devils proved a stumbling block. BBC Sport report that even though United's recruitment staff had been told that signing De Jong was impossible, Erik ten Hag was certain it could be done, dragging out the saga for the best part of two months.

De Jong's stance never changed and after two losses in Ten Hag's first two games, United were forced to pivot. They coughed up £70m to sign a 30-year-old Casemiro and handed him a bumper four-year contract.

‌



It feels apt that in the summer Casemiro departed, the new Old Trafford hierarchy are showing that they've learned from their predecessors' mistakes. Fans have been frustrated by the lack of updates since signing Tielemans on July 14, but in reality United have worked hard to keep a low profile and maintain a stealthy approach.

Is Carlos Baleba a good signing for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester United will have to raise their bid for Carlos Baleba (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



It should be noted that there's still work to do on Baleba, with United's offer of £60m plus £5m in add-ons not being sufficient. Nevertheless, expect the Cameroon international to be a United player by deadline day.

United did the groundwork on Baleba last summer when Brighton quoted them an eye-watering £100m off the back of his star-making season, so they'll have saved a good chunk of money by being patient. And could their latest move also serve as a blueprint for next year?

The Red Devils would also like to sign Lewis Hall, but given that Newcastle have already sold several key players this summer, it's an unlikely outcome. In 12 months' time, though, Hall will be a year closer to the expiry of his current contract and potentially more attainable.
